title: A review that says NOT READY records as ready-to-merge and releases the close-out
description:
pxc attempt 9 answered NOT READY. The run closed the review tick and recorded, in decisions/1.json, verdict 'ready-to-merge' — the collect vocabulary's word — beside a NOT READY summary. Only the untriaged-findings hold stopped the close-out from proceeding.

Two separate problems, and the second is the dangerous one:

1. ticfac.job-result.review-epic.v1 has NO review-verdict field. rolejob.go holds a role tick only on needsHuman (BLOCKED / NEEDS_CONTEXT), so a review's actual judgement has nowhere to live and no effect.
2. The durable record therefore says 'ready-to-merge' about a review that said the opposite. That record is what a later reader, or an auditor, or a future close-out trusts. It can be read as an approval that was never given.

THIS BLOCKS aqm. The operator decided to stop holding runs for untriaged findings and carry them to the PR instead. The findings hold is currently the ONLY thing that stopped a NOT READY review from releasing the close-out. Remove it before fixing this, and an epic whose review says it is not ready hands itself over with a record that reads as approval.

Work:
- Add a review-verdict to the review-epic result contract, distinct from the collect vocabulary's merge verdict. They answer different questions and sharing one word is how this happened.
- Decide, and state, whether NOT READY holds the close-out or is carried to the PR. Either is defensible; silence is not.
- The recorded decision must never spell a NOT READY review as ready-to-merge, whatever is decided about holding.

From pxc, its own second-pass finding — the review found this about itself.
